Tags emit signals at one of a number of pre-defined high frequencies and are located by comparing the strength of the signal at multiple readers. 433 MHz signals are less sensitive to blocking or distortion, such as by water or metals, but make the location data less accurate.

Tags (usually a printed label) have integrated circuits, but no power. Readers emit UHF radio waves and energise tags within range, receiving back a portion of the energy as information. Tag location is determined by its proximity to a fixed reader.

How does tracking assets help in manufacturing logistics?

On its most basic level, tracking vital assets, whether they be raw materials, vehicles, machinery, tools, or people, can demystify the manufacturing process. By knowing where vital assets are at all times, one can build up a digital twin of a process, which can allow for greater oversight of the processes, predictive analytics, and consequence-free experimentation.
UWB RTLS in manufacturing logistics: Why is it better?
